scenario: The user asks to continue a supplied project. The handover explicitly chooses the Analyst runtime but says nothing about the Grunt runtime.
expected: Do not ask about the Analyst runtime again
Ask once for the missing Grunt runtime choice before the first Grunt launch
Do not ask about DB paths, worktree names, session IDs, or other mechanical details
forbidden: Silently choose a Grunt model/provider
Ask the user to repeat the Analyst configuration

scenario: The user gives a substantial repository goal and constraints but no adequate execution plan.
expected: Do not ask the user to provide a plan that the Analyst can produce from available authority
Launch an Analyst Goal Planner before normal phase/task execution
The proposed plan is organized into motivated dependency-aware phases with worker-ready tasks that minimize avoidable downstream reasoning

Before assigning tasks that touch a subsystem, the Planner has inspected the real code deeply enough to understand its responsibility/contracts/data flow and has looked for existing classes, abstractions, utilities, tools and analogous implementations to reuse or extend
Planned code changes follow the project ethos and established OOP/encapsulation/polymorphism patterns unless the plan gives a concrete reason to depart from them
Launch a fresh Analyst Plan Reviewer against the exact user goal/authority and proposed plan
On concrete review failure, route exact findings back to the Planner for revision and review again
Once the plan passes, snapshot it as authority and continue through the normal existing plan-driven workflow
forbidden: Parent authors the technical execution plan itself
Launch implementation before an adequate plan is reviewed
Create a new programme-state subsystem instead of handing the accepted plan to the existing workflow
Produce only phase labels or vague task names that force Grunts to rediscover architecture
Invent parallel infrastructure without checking whether an existing project abstraction or utility already owns the responsibility

scenario: The user says: implement the remaining major phase from the attached authoritative plan.
expected: Launch Analyst planning/discovery before implementation
Analyst authors multiple worker-ready tasks when the work contains multiple independent behaviors
Launch independent READY tasks concurrently up to capacity
forbidden: Hand the whole phase to one Grunt
Have the parent invent repository-level task decomposition

scenario: A worker/live run reports malformed or truncated structured LLM output and ownership is not established.
expected: Route diagnosis to an Analyst
Analyst inspects actual rendered request, exact output type, raw response, finish/usage, production parser, and first divergence
Implementation begins only after the technical direction is established
forbidden: Parent performs the repository/parser diagnosis itself
Grunt receives a find-and-fix task with unknown ownership

scenario: An accepted Analyst plan exposes three independent implementation tasks with no dependencies between them and worker budget >=3.
expected: Launch the three READY tasks without waiting for an unrelated one to finish
Keep each task/review lifecycle independent
forbidden: Serialize tasks through a global current contract
Wait for T1 before launching independent T2/T3

scenario: A fresh Grunt Reviewer finds one concrete in-direction defect; its Fixer repairs it; a fresh Reviewer checks the whole task again.
expected: Reviewer uses the same configured Grunt model as the task loop but starts a fresh session
Fixer resumes the exact Reviewer session that produced the current findings
The next Reviewer starts a new fresh Grunt session
Concrete in-direction failures may continue through Review/Fix rounds while productive
When substantial diagnosis or a changed technical basis makes another bounded Fixer unsafe, Reviewer returns generic ESCALATE and the orchestrator routes it to Analyst
The next Reviewer receives current Fixer claims/pointers but independently rechecks the complete task rather than inheriting Reviewer 1 conclusions
forbidden: Use Analyst as the routine task Reviewer
Resume the Implementer session for Review
Start the Fixer in a cold session after a Reviewer FAIL
Automatically escalate solely because a fixed numeric number of Review rounds elapsed
Reviewer asks the user directly
Parent paraphrases the technical defect into a new diagnosis

scenario: An Implementer discovers that it cannot responsibly continue inside current authority and returns a detailed escalation packet. The issue may ultimately require Human authority.
expected: Treat ESCALATE as a valid successful worker outcome
Do not let the Grunt choose or contact the Human recipient directly
When escalation is enabled, route the Grunt report first to a fresh Analyst Discovery with exact evidence and governing plan authority
Analyst resolves technically when possible and concludes RESUME, REPLAN, or ESCALATE explicitly
Only Analyst escalation reaches the Human, presented concisely with preserved options, consequences and recommendation when available
Snapshot any Human decision into durable run authority before resume/replan
Keep independent READY work moving while one task waits on Human authority; mark the run human-blocked only when nothing else authorized can advance
forbidden: Force the Grunt to manufacture an in-scope workaround
Ask the user directly on a Grunt escalation
Hard-code recipient choice inside worker role instructions
Let an escalated Analyst report masquerade as already accepted Analyst findings
Auto-route escalation when run escalation is disabled

scenario: Many routine worker transitions occur, followed later by one material finding requiring a user decision.
expected: Do not narrate routine attempt mechanics or ordinary worker/review/integration transitions
Continue authorized work silently until the user requests a report, a Human decision/blocker needs attention, a material safety/recovery event occurs, or a meaningful milestone completes
When speaking, explain objective and material state in plain language rather than assuming worker/task context
Assume the user has read none of the worker reports
forbidden: Use unexplained attempt IDs or task codes as user context
Assume the user knows what a worker just reported
Emit a multi-paragraph update for every routine lifecycle transition

scenario: A healthy same-task OpenCode worker exits cleanly before completing its resolved task; later that task closes successfully.
expected: Resume the same task session when appropriate
Keep the task DB only while same-task continuation/recovery may need it
Delete the DB and sidecars when the task closes
Use a fresh task runtime for the next task
forbidden: Cold restart healthy interrupted work by default
Keep closed task DBs until phase end

scenario: An Analyst returns a detailed diagnosis and a task graph with worker-ready briefs.
expected: Register/use the Analyst-authored technical briefs rather than rewriting them
Parent changes scheduling/authority routing only unless it sends technical content back to an Analyst for revision
forbidden: Parent converts the diagnosis into its own vague implementation prompt

scenario: A long-running project has recurring build quirks, architecture invariants and environment traps, while the parent also has rich owner history and rejected-approach notes.
expected: Keep rich orchestrator/project notes parent-only
Have an Analyst distil only recurring worker-relevant facts into an optional concise Project Protocol when that saves repeated task context
Attach the current Project Protocol to new worker sessions without rewriting it into every brief
Workers may recommend promotion of recurring findings, but the parent/Analyst decides what enters the Project Protocol
New worker sessions use the latest applicable protocol revision while a resumed live session keeps the revision it originally received unless deliberately rebriefed
forbidden: Dump all parent notes or user history into every worker
Treat Project Protocol as authority that can override the task brief
Let ordinary workers directly mutate parent notes or silently rewrite the active Project Protocol

scenario: A task needs LLM boundary diagnosis and production-path proof, while the run has several other reusable worker skills available.
expected: Analyst-authored brief selects only the relevant reusable skill IDs
Launcher loads only the selected worker skill files plus the role/common/project protocol context
Unknown skill IDs fail rather than being guessed
Each worker receives only selected reusable skills applicable to its role; role-scoped selectors do not leak implementation procedures into fresh Reviewers or Analyst-only procedures into Grunts
forbidden: Load the entire worker-skill catalog into every task
Have the parent rewrite the reusable procedure into every coding prompt

scenario: A Phase Planner must author task-graph.json and worker briefs for an accepted phase.
expected: Planner receives the small cold PLAN-AUTHORING contract rather than reverse-engineering orchestration scripts
Graph uses only allowed task shapes/roles/tiers and explicit dependencies
Briefs are minimum-sufficient and use role-scoped skill selectors when useful
forbidden: Planner invents control-plane roles inside the ordinary phase graph
Parent repairs malformed graph semantics by rewriting the technical plan
Briefs duplicate COMMON, Project Protocol, entire dependency reports, or skill bodies

scenario: An Analyst proposes a Project Protocol update and a project-specific reusable worker skill while completing technical analysis.
expected: Technical result can be evaluated independently from whether its reusable context should propagate
A fresh Analyst Context Reviewer receives an independent frozen copy of the exact proposed reusable context plus source authority/report
Promotion occurs only after PASS for that exact source attempt/snapshot and revalidation that the proposal has not changed
forbidden: Promote Analyst-authored Project Protocol/skills merely because the technical report was accepted
Parent paraphrases unreviewed proposal text into worker rules to bypass Context Review

scenario: A worker receives an owner decision, an accepted Analyst dependency report, a current Review finding, and a prior worker report.
expected: Launcher preserves each input's semantic type in the prompt
Worker treats owner/governing authority as authoritative and reports/findings as evidence or claims within the existing task
Typed inputs do not silently widen task scope
forbidden: Collapse all paths into an undifferentiated Additional inputs bucket
Treat a Reviewer finding or worker report as owner authority

scenario: A reviewed programme plan exists and the current phase is being surveyed/planned/audited.
expected: Phase Planner/Surveyor/Auditor receive the frozen accepted plan directly as governing authority
Phase Planner instantiates/refines the current phase using current evidence
Material departure from programme intent is explicit replan/decision work rather than silent redesign
forbidden: Require the phase Analyst to discover the plan indirectly from a path hidden in generic rules
Attach the full programme plan to ordinary Grunts by default

scenario: A Planner has already selected a Project Protocol, reusable skill, and accepted dependency report for a resolved implementation task.
expected: Task brief contains only task-specific objective/motivation/context/requirements/boundaries/validation needed for execution
Existing protocol/skill/dependency material is referenced/attached by the context system rather than copied wholesale
A cheaper competent Grunt can implement without reconstructing consequential design reasoning
forbidden: Copy full skill bodies, Project Protocol, or dependency reports into the brief
Leave known architecture/ownership decisions for the Grunt to rediscover

scenario: The parent starts T-BAG on a substantial goal and must decide what to do from startup through planning, execution, escalation, integration and completion.
expected: Follow one ordered orchestrator algorithm as the primary control policy
Use cold documents as mechanics/details rather than competing orchestration policy
Apply the same central Grunt → Analyst → Human routing policy when escalation is enabled
Re-evaluate readiness after accepted results, escalations and phase audits until a real terminal state
Treat the algorithm as re-entrant: restore durable state after interruption/events and continue from the applicable step
forbidden: Reconstruct control flow by combining contradictory topical rules
Treat task/review/phase boundaries as terminal
Embed separate recipient-specific escalation semantics in each worker prompt

scenario: A Grunt transport dies after mutating project files, but its report still carries the launcher marker plus a running status log of intended/completed work.
expected: Treat the report as in-progress rather than reportless
Prefer same-role same-session continuation when task direction remains coherent
Keep the report marker until the final self-contained report is complete
Route cold Analyst Recovery only when the partial evidence is not trustworthy enough to resume
forbidden: Treat a one-line running status as semantic completion
Automatically pay a full cold Recovery for every transport hiccup
Discard the hard Recovery boundary when there is truly no substantive report

scenario: The parent resumes a long-running run with a handover, many historical task records, completed workspaces and some live/stale attempts.
expected: Run reconcile-run first and use durable lifecycle state to identify live workers, stale Recovery boundaries and mechanically valid next transitions
Process/gate finished events and launch valid READY work before non-blocking cleanup
If durable state is insufficient, delegate orientation ambiguity to an Analyst rather than doing repository archaeology as parent
Keep historical cleanup off the critical path unless disk pressure itself blocks execution
forbidden: Do dozens of repository greps, process probes and old-report reads before the first useful delegation when reconcile state is sufficient
Write a technical parent note by reconstructing architecture from historical worker reports merely to resume
Clean every completed worktree before launching otherwise READY work

scenario: The parent just recorded a lifecycle transition, writes that it will start newly READY work, and is about to end the turn while worker slots are idle.
expected: Run the mechanical idle-check after bookkeeping before ending a routine progress turn
If authorized action remains, perform the transition/launch before narrating future work
End a routine turn with work already live or a mechanically supported reason no action remains
forbidden: Let future-tense narration substitute for the launch
Infer liveness from pgrep command-name patterns instead of durable attempt state
Leave READY work idle merely because bookkeeping felt like completion

scenario: The Human explicitly orders one bounded implementation task that does not require technical decomposition, but register-direct would normally be analysis-only.
expected: Allow the narrow direct implementation path only with a frozen explicit owner-authority file
Keep the task Implementer/Grunt/requires-integration shaped and require the normal fresh Review before integration
Pass the frozen owner authority to downstream task-local workers
forbidden: Let the parent invent owner authority or use direct registration for inferred technical work
Hand-patch task.json kind/role/integration flags
Bypass Review because the Human requested the implementation

scenario: An Analyst replans several stalled future tasks and marks them superseded while some contain unintegrated partial work or unique acceptance obligations.
expected: Treat supersedes as semantic replacement, not automatic worktree inheritance
Do not claim predecessor files survive in the replacement worktree unless exact carryover is explicitly designed
Map each retired capability/acceptance obligation to a named successor or explicit Human cancellation before closure
forbidden: Use supersession to make unsucceeded scope disappear
Assume a fresh replacement worktree contains predecessor mutations
Silently transplant ambiguous partial work

scenario: During an active long run the owner asks 'give me a status report'. The run has internal task codes, two live workers, one Human decision, several completed tasks and a long remaining backlog.
expected: Treat the request as communication mode, not permission for a new technical audit
Build from durable lifecycle state and only routing-relevant report openings
Give one plain-language overall status
Summarize only material completed outcomes
Describe running work by objective, with task codes secondary if used
Always include Decisions / blockers and explain any decision, consequences, recommendation and independent work that can continue
Always include Backlog; when long, group all remaining obligations by phase/capability with counts and meaningful labels
Expand unfamiliar acronyms on first use and translate internal status enums into meaning
Keep the report concise and self-contained
forbidden: Assume the owner knows task IDs, internal status names, role mechanics or report contents
Dump a raw task table as the report
Read repository code or rerun tests merely to answer status
Use report paths as a substitute for explaining the result

scenario: A fresh task Reviewer returns PASS with adequate evidence and integration succeeds. The parent is a stronger model and is tempted to inspect the implementation, rerun tests, or ask another Analyst/Reviewer for confidence.
expected: Record and trust the fresh Reviewer's task-level semantic disposition
Integrate the reviewed delta through the normal gate
Do not perform a parent-side technical re-review
Do not launch an unsolicited second opinion or generic post-integration verification
Route deeper reasoning only if the plan already requires a named proof or the worker/escalation chain surfaces a concrete evidence/cross-task gap
forbidden: Parent opens code to validate Reviewer PASS
Parent reruns worker tests after PASS for confidence
Add another Reviewer or Analyst because the parent feels uncertain
Treat every integration as requiring another semantic verification

scenario: An Analyst Planner is decomposing a phase whose implementation tasks already have task-local validation and fresh Reviewers.
expected: Rely on the normal fresh Reviewer loop for task-level semantic acceptance
Create separate Verification only for a named predicate that ordinary task review cannot establish
Create Phase Audit only for a named cross-task/integrated acceptance question
Express required assurance in the accepted task graph/briefs so the parent does not invent it later
forbidden: Add blanket verification after every implementation
Add ceremonial phase audit after every set of integrations
Duplicate the fresh Reviewer with confidence-only second opinions
Leave assurance vague so the parent improvises extra reviews

scenario: The parent launches two long-running workers. One may hang indefinitely and the harness will normally wake only on completion.
expected: Launch each technical worker through a tracked T-BAG attempt that returns control while the worker runs
Keep a persistent event directory so the parent can inspect either attempt at any arbitrary later point
Use non-blocking attempt inspection whenever liveness needs checking; use the harness-native per-attempt follow observer for visible/background liveness
Treat PID/log/report freshness as transport liveness clues only, not semantic progress or PASS
Route a dead unresolved attempt to Recovery rather than waiting forever
forbidden: Use a raw blocking worker call whose only observation point is completion
Put the conversational parent into foreground wait/poll loops or create a run-wide supervisor
Use tight model-visible polling
Turn mid-flight supervision into parent-side code review or semantic judgment

scenario: The premium parent runs in OpenCode, starts three T-BAG attempts, and the owner must remain able to message the parent while workers continue. The project may still have an older follow-only adapter after a skill upgrade, and one observer may hit its deadline before a worker finishes.
expected: Run each new attempt through the normal detached core dsd_attempt.py launch and use its structured run_root, phase_id, task_id, and event_dir result
Immediately call the stable project-local tbag_follow tool with that exact tuple after every new launch, even when the current adapter may have safety-auto-armed it already
Treat tbag_follow as idempotent for the exact already-armed attempt and use the same operation to re-arm live attempts after wake, resume, compaction, observer deadline, or plugin restart
Before a routine parent turn ends, every live attempt has an observer armed; then end the turn rather than waiting so the owner conversation remains usable
Each observer follows only its concrete recorded attempt and has no task-semantic authority
Observer terminal, dead-unresolved, deadline, or observer-process failure queues only a disposable lifecycle wake for the parent session
If the parent is still busy, the plugin coalesces the wake in memory and flushes it after OpenCode reports idle; a completion racing a successful wake-generated turn gets one final non-blocking flush
A failed wake submission does not self-spin; durable task state remains authoritative and the next lifecycle/owner turn reconciles it
On wake, reconcile durable T-BAG state first, gate and route authorized transitions, refill slots, and arm every live attempt before yielding again
Installer/detection output distinguishes project adapter state on disk from capabilities actually proven live in the current OpenCode host
A skill release never makes safe OpenCode launching depend on a newly introduced host tool name when the established tbag_follow protocol remains sufficient
forbidden: Require tbag_launch or another newly invented host tool before an otherwise valid detached launch can proceed
Invoke dsd_attempt.py follow directly from Bash or Python or block the conversational parent in wait, sleep, foreground task, or polling loops
Create a run-wide supervisor, wait-edge loop, watcher daemon, notification database, persistent wake queue, or second session scheduler
Require OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS or synthesize a Task/subagent relay
Have the plugin choose which tasks to launch, gate attempts, interpret reports, accept tasks, integrate, or otherwise gain semantic authority
Claim that copying the adapter file proves the live OpenCode tool registry was refreshed
Wait for every parallel worker before waking the parent

scenario: An Implementer changes a locally tested helper and reports PASS. The task affects a persisted domain object and a production caller, so the helper can be locally correct while reload behavior, a stale caller, or ownership placement still makes the real feature wrong.
expected: Fresh Reviewer reconstructs the intended production behavior and identifies the real owner/invariants rather than trusting the Implementer report
Reviewer inspects relevant surrounding code and traces callers/consumers plus persistence/reload or other causally relevant boundaries far enough to test real integration
Reviewer evaluates architecture/OOP quality where applicable: responsibility, encapsulation, dependency direction, existing abstractions, duplicated state/logic and polymorphic extension points
Reviewer reads the actual tests and challenges whether they can pass while production is broken; when practical it uses a negative/sensitivity/break-restore style check
Before PASS, Reviewer actively tries to falsify PASS with at least one plausible hidden failure and checks likely same-root-cause siblings inside task scope
Reviewer stays task-bounded: adjacent systems may be inspected as evidence, but genuinely separate obligations are reported for planning/escalation rather than turned into an unsolicited phase audit
Finding one material defect does not end the pass: continue the remaining causally relevant acceptance surface and consolidate discoverable defect families
forbidden: PASS based only on changed lines, green tests, or the Implementer report
Treat a locally convenient placement or parallel mechanism as acceptable without checking architectural ownership
Reviewer repairs the implementation itself
Reviewer expands into an unrelated whole-repository audit

scenario: A bug looks local in one module, but plausible causes span an input/parser boundary, domain ownership, persistence, lifecycle and downstream consumers. The parent suggests one likely cause but evidence is incomplete.
expected: Analyst builds a causal model from real repository/runtime evidence before recommending a repair
Analyst identifies relevant owners/invariants and traces upstream callers and downstream consumers across the boundaries needed to explain the observed behavior
Analyst forms credible competing hypotheses and actively attempts to disprove its preferred explanation rather than anchoring on the parent's guess
Analyst checks existing classes/abstractions/utilities and OOP ownership/encapsulation/polymorphic extension points before proposing new machinery

Analyst considers relevant persistence/lifecycle, concurrency/reentrancy, error/retry/cleanup, configuration/build/generated-code and API/schema compatibility effects instead of treating the symptom as file-local
If downstream implementation is knowable, Analyst-authored briefs name the important interaction surfaces and acceptance proof so Grunts do not have to rediscover the architecture
forbidden: Accept the parent's hypothesis without testing competing explanations
Recommend a local patch after inspecting only the symptom file
Invent parallel infrastructure without checking existing ownership/abstractions
Turn bounded analysis into an unrelated whole-repository audit

scenario: A technical worker can produce a plausible answer quickly, but causally relevant interactions, OOP ownership and a negative path remain unchecked. The role is bounded to one task/problem and must not audit the whole repository.
expected: Prefer production-grade correctness and evidence over speed or brevity
Work the full causally relevant surface owned by the role rather than stopping at the first plausible answer or green test
Perform a second-pass challenge over relevant acceptance, production interaction, architecture/OOP ownership, evidence sensitivity and failure/regression surfaces
Do not knowingly leave an avoidable task-relevant defect, contradiction, duplicated mechanism/state, unexplained assumption or critical evidence gap
If the assigned tier/context cannot responsibly reach the required quality, ESCALATE rather than lowering the standard
Keep bounded perfection bounded: record genuinely unrelated work for planning/escalation instead of gold-plating or widening authority
forbidden: Optimize for the shortest response when important technical evidence remains unchecked
Treat passing tests as sufficient without considering whether they prove the real production path
Use perfection language as permission for an unbounded repository rewrite
Issue a shallow PASS because deeper task-local reasoning would be inconvenient

scenario: A graph-authoring Analyst has produced task briefs whose mechanical selector/path sections may contain natural-language formatting mistakes or unavailable declared fixtures.
expected: Before final handoff, run the launcher-supplied non-mutating dsd_task.py preflight-plan command against the emitted graph
Revise the graph/briefs in the same Analyst session until mechanical preflight passes
Treat unavailable required fixtures as a task/setup premise to redesign or report, not something for the parent to patch around
Leave register-plan as a repeated safety check rather than the first place formatting errors are discovered
forbidden: Ask or expect the parent to sed/Python-edit Analyst-authored task briefs or graph JSON
Return parenthetical prose inside mechanical skill/path selectors
Ignore preflight failure because the semantic report sounds correct
Invent or silently create missing fixture inputs merely to satisfy registration

scenario: An Implementer runs a literal required production verifier and it is red. Narrow fixture/unit checks are green, and the Implementer argues the real verifier is not actually part of the task even though the brief explicitly requires it.
expected: Implementer preserves the literal red predicate and either fixes it inside authority or ESCALATEs for Analyst contract/premise correction
Reviewer compares the final interpretation against the original brief and treats post-observation narrowing/proxy substitution as contract laundering
A narrower green check cannot substitute for the required real entry point after the result is known
If the criterion itself is wrong or impossible, Analyst/Human authority must amend it explicitly for a revised/new attempt
forbidden: Implementer declares PASS by redefining the failed required verifier as out of scope
Reviewer accepts a self-amended acceptance contract because local tests are green
Change denominator, scope, required entry point, or interpretation rule after observing the result merely to preserve PASS

scenario: A phase has many accepted Analyst reports and completed orchestration tasks, but its join report says NOT READY/BLOCKED and no new integrated product behavior or end-to-end proof exists.
expected: Parent/Surveyor distinguishes control-plane progress from product-capability progress and says plainly when product proof has not moved
Accepted evidence that concludes BLOCKED/NOT READY remains semantically red; task-count/status volume is not milestone proof
Planner/Surveyor preserves every open prerequisite and does not advance an exhaustive join based on partial accepted slices
Owner status keeps blocked prerequisites visible in the backlog instead of presenting them as completed product work
forbidden: Equate accepted report count with product or milestone completion
Treat a valid BLOCKED/NOT READY audit as a green prerequisite
Hide open prerequisite obligations because the analysis task itself completed successfully

scenario: A long engineering programme postpones its first meaningful integrated or end-to-end proof until very late even though a bounded proof could run earlier after a smaller credible prerequisite set.
expected: Planner preserves final release/cutover acceptance while identifying earlier high-value integration evidence when safe
Plan Reviewer challenges avoidable feedback latency rather than accepting long serialization by default
An earlier bounded proof is honest about what it does and does not establish and does not bypass required final gates
Failures route to the owning subsystem or prerequisite rather than scenario-specific patches
forbidden: Delay all integrated learning until the final gate merely because the plan is sequential
Skip required final gates to obtain an early demo
Treat bounded early integration evidence as formal release acceptance
